overall_summary: Bitcoin faces clear selling pressure as Binance hack fallout drives heavy outflows, ETF redemptions, and potential large holder sales. Hawkish Fed signals and sticky inflation keep macro support weak, while Iran strike risks and G20 discord add risk-off tone. Near-term catalysts lean toward further downside until flows stabilize.
key_points: Binance hack sparks billions in outflows
Fed holds rates but officials eye hikes
Nasdaq firm may sell or pledge BTC
Iran strike talk lifts geopolitical risk

items.title: Binance Resumes Phased Withdrawals After $6.3B Hack
items.summary: Binance has started reopening customer withdrawals in phases on Sunday, beginning with Bitcoin and covering 15 networks, after covering about 95 percent of the record 6.3 billion dollar theft from its hot wallets. The exchange is absorbing the losses itself using corporate funds, SAFU reserves, and other sources, and says major assets like BTC, ETH, and stables are now fully backed with a new proof-of-reserves snapshot. Traders should watch for potential large outflows as users regain access, which could pressure prices short-term even as the coverage calms solvency fears.
items.impact: Reduces existential FUD but risks temporary selling pressure from withdrawals

items.title: FBI Pins Binance Hack on North Korea TraderTraitor
items.summary: The FBI confirmed North Korea's TraderTraitor group stole more than 6 billion dollars from Binance on or about October 29, urging DeFi platforms, exchanges, and node operators to block listed BTC, ETH, and SOL addresses tied to the laundering. Hackers have been converting assets mainly into Ethereum and are expected to use DeFi and swaps further. This official attribution heightens geopolitical and sanctions risk awareness for the whole sector and may slow recovery of stolen funds.
items.impact: Amplifies state-actor and compliance overhang on crypto markets

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $643M Single-Day Outflow
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded 643 million dollars in net outflows on October 30, the largest daily redemption in months, wiping out the prior four-day inflow streak and leaving October with roughly 516 million dollars in net withdrawals. BlackRock IBIT and Fidelity FBTC led the exits. This institutional selling forced real BTC sales to meet redemptions and signals caution amid the Binance fallout and broader risk-off moves.
items.impact: Direct selling pressure from ETF redemptions into the market

items.title: Nasdaq Firm May Sell or Pledge $450M in Bitcoin
items.summary: Next Technology Holding, a small Nasdaq-listed company, authorized its CEO to sell or borrow against its entire 5,833 BTC holdings worth roughly 450 million dollars, citing the Binance hack, exchange risks, and quantum computing threats even though none of its coins were on Binance. The firm's market cap is only about 8 million dollars, making the stash vastly larger than its equity. Any actual sales or loans could add meaningful supply overhang if executed.
items.impact: Potential large corporate BTC distribution into weak market

items.title: Billions Flow Out of Binance After Withdrawals Restart
items.summary: Shortly after Binance reopened withdrawals, on-chain trackers reported 1 to 2 billion dollars in net outflows, with users moving funds off the platform. Binance also used part of its SAFU bitcoin reserve to help cover remaining illiquid stolen assets. This flight-to-self-custody is classic post-hack behavior and can create near-term liquidity and price pressure even as the exchange stabilizes.
items.impact: Short-term exchange outflow and selling pressure

items.title: Hacker Converts Stolen SOL Toward Bitcoin
items.summary: On-chain monitors show the Binance attacker moving and converting large amounts of the stolen 970,000-plus SOL, worth tens of millions, into Bitcoin via protocols like Relay in recent hours. Earlier dumps of thinner tokens already crashed some prices 90 percent. Continued laundering and conversion of the haul keeps supply risk alive and can spill into BTC order books.
items.impact: Ongoing stolen-fund conversion adds sell-side pressure

items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady at 3.75-4% With Two Dissents
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept the federal funds rate unchanged in a 10-2 vote last Wednesday, with Governors Cook and Hammack preferring a quarter-point hike. Chair Kevin Warsh stressed that inflation remains elevated and more data will guide the next move, while upgrading the economy's pace to strong. Traders still price high odds of a December hike. Crypto traders should watch this closely because a patient but still hawkish Fed keeps financial conditions tight and supports the dollar.
items.impact: Supports higher-for-longer rates and dollar strength, pressuring risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: Q3 GDP Beats at 3.4 Percent as PCE Inflation Stays Sticky
items.summary: Third-quarter US GDP grew at a strong 3.4 percent annualized rate, driven by consumer spending and AI-related investment. September PCE inflation came in elevated around 3.6 percent year-over-year with core near 3.1 percent. The combination of solid growth and persistent prices reinforces the case for the Fed to stay restrictive. This mix typically weighs on liquidity-sensitive assets like crypto until inflation clearly cools.
items.impact: Bolsters December rate-hike odds and keeps real yields elevated

items.title: Fed Officials Musalem and Logan Call for More Hikes Soon
items.summary: St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem and Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan spoke Friday saying additional firming is needed, with Logan pointing to at least two more quarter-point increases. Their comments came right after the hold and hot data. Markets are taking this as confirmation that the pause is temporary. For Bitcoin traders this raises the bar for any near-term risk-on relief.
items.impact: Increases probability of further tightening into year-end

items.title: Bank of Japan Holds at 1.25 Percent, Declares 2% Target Met
items.summary: The BOJ left its policy rate unchanged on Friday in an 8-1 vote but said underlying inflation is now consistent with its 2 percent goal for the first time since 2013. It raised its 2027 inflation forecast and sped up ETF sales, while signaling readiness for more hikes. This is a major milestone after years of ultra-easy policy. Yen strength or further BOJ tightening could spill into global yields and dollar dynamics that matter for crypto.
items.impact: Potential yen support and global rate spillover; watch USD/JPY

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Eases Toward 4.93 Percent, DXY Holds Near 102
items.summary: Treasury yields pulled back late in the week, with the 10-year closing around 4.93 to 4.94 percent after touching higher levels earlier, partly on tech-driven safe-haven flows. The dollar index hovered near 101.7 to 102, still firm on relative rate and growth differentials. Bond markets are digesting the Fed hold against sticky inflation. Softening yields offer limited relief for risk assets but the dollar remains a headwind for Bitcoin.
items.impact: Modest easing in yields supportive at the margin; strong dollar still restrictive

items.title: No Major US Data Today; ISM Manufacturing Due Monday, NFP Friday
items.summary: Sunday brings no scheduled US economic releases. Markets will focus tomorrow on the ISM Manufacturing PMI, then JOLTS midweek and the big October jobs report on Friday. Consensus leans toward continued expansion but softish payrolls. Crypto traders should treat the week as data-heavy with potential volatility around any surprise that shifts Fed path odds.
items.impact: Sets up key catalysts that could reprice rate expectations and risk appetite

items.title: Trump Eyes Quick Iran Strikes; Tehran Warns Unrestricted Retaliation
items.summary: President Trump said the US has knocked out most of Iran's military but still needs to take care of one or two targets, including a suspected nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain, and could do it in ten minutes. Iran's supreme leader ordered an immediate, geographically unrestricted response to any new attack and updated target lists. Qatari-mediated talks continue with a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in two days if US conditions are met, but tanker incidents and strike fears persist right before US midterms. Traders should watch oil prices and risk assets closely because any escalation would spike energy costs and drive broad risk-off moves.
items.impact: Higher oil, elevated volatility and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: G20 Ministers End Atlanta Talks Without Joint Statement
items.summary: G20 foreign ministers wrapped two days in Atlanta with no consensus joint declaration due to deep splits over Ukraine, the US-Iran war, tariffs and China. The traditional group photo was cancelled after Europeans refused to stand with Russia's Lavrov. The US did approve a 2.1 billion dollar Patriot interceptor sale to Ukraine. This underscores fractured global coordination on security and energy routes just ahead of the leaders summit and midterms, keeping uncertainty high for markets.
items.impact: Sustained geopolitical risk premium and supply-chain/energy uncertainty

items.title: FBI Links North Korea to Record 6.3 Billion Binance Hack
items.summary: The FBI confirmed North Korea's TraderTraitor group stole more than 6 billion dollars in crypto from Binance around October 29, the largest such heist on record. Binance said it has already covered about 90 percent of losses from its own funds and is resuming withdrawals in phases. The regime is converting assets mainly to Ethereum for further laundering. For crypto traders this highlights persistent state-sponsored theft risk that can hit confidence and liquidity even when exchanges make users whole.
items.impact: Short-term crypto confidence hit and heightened sanctions/cyber scrutiny

items.title: Israel Election Deadlock Leaves No Clear Majority
items.summary: Final counts from Israel's October 27 election leave Netanyahu's bloc with 53 seats, the main opposition at 48 and Arab-led parties at a record 19, short of the 61 needed for a majority. Coalition talks will be messy with both sides ruling out key partners, raising chances of prolonged caretaker rule or another election. This political uncertainty hits a key US ally in the middle of the Iran conflict and could slow decision-making on regional security.
items.impact: Added Middle East policy uncertainty pending coalition outcome

items.title: US Approves 2.1 Billion Patriot Sale to Ukraine Amid G20 Rifts
items.summary: While G20 talks fractured, the State Department cleared a proposed 2.1 billion dollar sale of Patriot air-defence interceptors to Ukraine. Zelensky welcomed the move but wants faster delivery. It comes against continued Russian strikes and mixed US-Russia signalling under Trump. The package offers some defensive boost for Kyiv but does not resolve the larger war or energy-market spill-overs from the conflict.
items.impact: Limited positive for Ukraine defence; little immediate broad market relief

items.title: Melania-Brokered Oleshky Ceasefire Enables Ukraine Evacuations
items.summary: A localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, brokered by First Lady Melania Trump, has allowed humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations, with residents arriving in Ukrainian-held territory. Both sides honoured the temporary halt for the mission in the devastated Kherson-area city. It is a rare de-escalation bright spot but remains confined to one location while the wider war and energy infrastructure strikes continue.
items.impact: Minor positive humanitarian signal; no material change to broader war risk
